The work of architectural and engineering managers can be divided into four categories: project planning and objectives and scope management (defining project scope and objectives and main deliverables, preparing budget and schedule and resource plans, assessing technical and resource and market feasibility, and presenting and explaining options and reports to clients); cross-disciplinary coordination and team and personnel management (coordinating engineering and R&D disciplines and external stakeholders, organizing reviews and decisions, and guiding recruitment and deployment and evaluation of project personnel); technical and standards and compliance management (formulating or implementing policies and standards or procedures for engineering and technical work, approving design changes, and enforcing regulations and technical standards and quality and safety requirements); and sustainability and environmental impact management (assessing the environmental impact of engineering and R&D activities, formulating or implementing options to improve sustainability or reduce environmental impact, and tracking environmental regulations and social pressure to support decisions).

values: Practice materials: fictional equipment testing project

Budget ceiling 100 wan yuan, approved baseline 95 wan yuan, and the 5 wan yuan margin must not be spent automatically without approval; the baseline includes a non-reducible 5 wan yuan safety and environmental inspection. The objective is to deliver acceptance-tested testing equipment by the end of working day 14; this exercise does not involve real construction.

Activity A requirement freeze 2 days, B equipment procurement 5 days, C installation 4 days, D testing 3 days, E personnel training 4 days; B and E must start after A, C must start after B, and D must start after both C and E are finished. After A the two branches have independent personnel and can run in parallel; all activity durations are in working days, and the start point is day 0.

Update: B is extended from 5 days to 7 days, and its cost is expected to increase by 4 wan yuan; other durations and costs are unchanged. The supplier can be paid an extra 2 wan yuan to restore B to 5 days; this does not change the safety, quality, and acceptance requirements.

The client still requires delivery on day 14 and no additional budget, and additionally wants to add a remote dashboard: an extra 6 wan yuan, with activity F taking 2 days and starting after D is finished. The dashboard is not in the original scope and can be approved separately with a delay; the client also suggests deleting the 5 wan yuan safety and environmental inspection.

The engineering lead confirms: acceptance of the original scope requires both D testing and the safety and environmental inspection to pass; the inspection runs in parallel with stage D and cannot be deleted. Procurement is carried out by the procurement lead, installation and testing by the engineering team, and training by the training lead; the manager has no authority to exceed 100 wan yuan or lower the acceptance standards. All figures are given by the editors and are not regulatory engineering quotas.
Deliverables
Write a one-page charter: objectives, original scope, acceptance, budget ceiling, and authority; list activity dependencies, responsible persons, and risks.

Calculate the duration, critical path, and expected total cost for the baseline, the delay, and the acceleration; judge the two requests for the remote dashboard and the inspection cut, and list the items that require approval.

Write a reply of no more than 500 characters to the client, stating the options, remaining budget, delivery date, acceptance, and approval conditions; do not claim that the manager can directly decide beyond authority.
Reference calculations and handling

Baseline A-B-C-D totals 2+5+4+3=14 days; A-E-D is 2+4+3=9 days. E finishes on day 6, C finishes on day 11, and D runs from day 11 to day 14, so the critical path is A-B-C-D; the baseline cost is 95 wan yuan with a margin of 5 wan yuan.

After B is delayed, the critical path is 2+7+4+3=16 days and the expected cost is 95+4=99 wan yuan, below the ceiling but 2 days late. After paying the acceleration fee, B returns to 5 days and the duration is 14 days, with a cost of 95+4+2=101 wan yuan, exceeding the ceiling by 1 wan yuan; without additional budget, the original scope and the 14-day deadline cannot both be met.

With the dashboard added: without acceleration it is 105 wan yuan and 18 days; with acceleration it is 107 wan yuan and 16 days. Both exceed the budget and are late. The inspection cannot be deleted; it is recommended that the client approve the original scope at 16 days and 99 wan yuan and postpone the dashboard. If 14 days is mandatory, at least 1 wan yuan must be formally added and the acceleration approved; the dashboard requires a separate change review and additional budget.

Sample reply: the original scope is currently expected to cost 99 wan yuan and take 16 working days, 2 days later than the target. Accelerating procurement can restore 14 days, but the total would be 101 wan yuan, exceeding the budget ceiling by 1 wan yuan, and execution requires your approval of the additional budget and the change. The remote dashboard is not in the original scope and would add another 6 wan yuan and 2 days, so it is recommended to approve it separately in a later phase. The safety and environmental inspection and the original acceptance requirements are retained. Please confirm either the delay option or the additional-budget option; before approval, expenditures remain controlled under the original authorization, and the procurement, plan, and acceptance versions are recorded.

paragraphs: Mainland China: the registered constructor system targets the corresponding construction management practice. Without obtaining a registration certificate and practice seal, one may not serve as the project leader of the construction unit for large and medium-sized construction projects; this is not a uniform entry condition for all engineering managers. Positions in design, R&D, and manufacturing shall have their professional qualifications and authority separately verified according to actual duties, and a constructor certificate is not to be treated as a design seal qualification.

Construction practice details: Article 10 of the Regulations on the Administration of Registered Constructors provides that the certificate and seal are valid for 3 years; Article 20 requires the construction leader to be employed and registered with an enterprise that holds construction qualifications; Article 21 provides that the specific scope follows the practice project scale standards, and one may not serve as the project leader of the construction unit on two or more projects at the same time; Article 22 requires construction management and quality acceptance documents to be sealed as prescribed; Article 23 requires 60 credit hours each of required and elective continuing education per validity period. Articles 25 and 26 also provide for quality responsibility, confidentiality, recusal, and the prohibition of false documents and lending certificates or seals.
